## Overview

The term project is your chance to apply the tools from this course to a dataset you care about - ideally data from your own lab or rotation. You will process a large dataset on Talapas, analyze it in R or Python, and write up what you did as a reproducible Quarto document. It is worth 40% of the course grade: 5% for the proposal and 35% for the final project.

## Part 1 - Project proposal (5%)

**Assigned:** Monday, October 26 · **Due:** Monday, November 9, 2026 (by midnight, via Canvas)

Write a short proposal (about one page, submitted as a rendered Quarto document) that answers:

1.  **The data.** What dataset will you use? Where does it come from, how big is it (files, rows, GB), and what format is it in? If you do not have data of your own, say so - I will help you choose a public dataset (see the [data repositories](../book/chapters/appendix-C-data-formats.html) appendix) or you can use the course stickleback RNA-seq data.
2.  **The question.** What is the one scientific or technical question you want to answer with it?
3.  **The plan.** Which steps will run at the shell, which in R or Python, and which on Talapas? A five-to-ten line sketch of the pipeline is plenty.
4.  **What you expect to learn.** One or two sentences.

The proposal is not binding - it is a way to catch problems (data too big, wrong format, no Talapas access) while there is still time to fix them.

## Part 2 - Final project (35%)

**Assignment:** Details to follow after the proposals are in.

**Due:** Submit your work via Canvas by the end of the day (midnight) on **Friday, December 11th, 2026.**
